prohibited_recommendations: Do not administer corticosteroids as monotherapy — they are ineffective in GBS and may worsen outcome.
Do not combine IVIG and plasma exchange in sequence — no additive benefit and increased adverse events.
Avoid sedating medications that depress respiratory drive while FVC is declining.
Do not start IVIG without checking renal function and IgA status.
required_recommendations: Admit to a monitored unit (step-down or ICU) given FVC 58% predicted and NIF -28 cmH2O — both approaching intubation thresholds.
Repeat FVC, MIP/MEP, and NIF every 4 hours and intubate if FVC <20 mL/kg, NIF worse than -30 cmH2O, or VC <40% predicted (20-30-40 rule).
Start IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (or plasma exchange) within 2 weeks of symptom onset.
Continuous cardiac telemetry for autonomic arrhythmias.
Start mechanical / pharmacologic DVT prophylaxis appropriate for an immobilised inpatient.

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome, AIDP subtype, post-Campylobacter jejuni

differential.key_features: Indistinguishable from AIDP at 10 days; differentiation requires longitudinal course (>8 weeks progression) or relapse — current course too short to confirm.
Sensory level and sphincter dysfunction absent; areflexia rather than hyperreflexia; spinal MRI shows nerve-root rather than cord involvement.

differential.diagnosis: Acute polyradiculoneuropathy from Lyme / other infection
differential.key_features: Possible mimic but Campylobacter serology positive and no tick exposure / endemic travel reported.
Pattern is ascending, not descending; sensory paresthesias prominent; EMG demyelinating, not low-amplitude with incremental RNS response.
Facial diplegia present but reflexes are preserved in MG; no fatigability pattern; EMG demyelinating.

key_clinical_evidence: Ascending symmetric weakness + areflexia + bilateral facial diplegia + antecedent Campylobacter = classic AIDP per Brighton level 1.
CSF protein 78 mg/dL with WBC 3/μL is the expected albuminocytologic dissociation; cell count <10/μL distinguishes from infection-driven polyradiculitis.
EMG/NCS pattern (prolonged DML, reduced CV, absent F-waves, absent sural SNAPs) confirms demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy.
Anti-GM1 / anti-GD1a IgG positivity following Campylobacter raises the possibility of secondary axonal involvement — repeat EMG in 1–2 weeks for prognostication.
Respiratory monitoring drives disposition: FVC 58% with NIF -28 cmH2O is unstable and mandates ICU-capable care.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Inflammatory signature is the trailing footprint of the antecedent C. jejuni illness 3 weeks earlier; it does not point to active CNS or systemic infection.
red_herrings.data_point: Mild leukocytosis (WBC 11.2) with elevated CRP and ESR
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggest active systemic infection or sepsis as the primary driver of weakness rather than post-infectious autoimmune polyradiculoneuropathy.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Diffuse nerve-root enhancement is a recognised finding in AIDP and supports — rather than contradicts — the GBS diagnosis when interpreted in context.
red_herrings.data_point: Cauda equina nerve-root enhancement on lumbosacral MRI
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggest an inflammatory or neoplastic radiculopathy (e.g., neurosarcoidosis, leptomeningeal disease) requiring tissue diagnosis.

sequence_constraints.reason: Document respiratory status (FVC/NIF) before committing to IVIG vs plasma exchange — severe respiratory compromise mandates ICU triage and may influence treatment choice and timing.
Renal function, IgA screen, and CBC must be reviewed before IVIG to mitigate renal failure, anaphylaxis (IgA-deficient patients), and aseptic meningitis risk.

specialized_test.impression: This is an ABNORMAL nerve conduction study. 1. Markedly prolonged distal motor latencies and reduced conduction velocities in bilateral median and peroneal motor nerves. 2. Absent sural sensory nerve action potentials bilaterally. 3. Electrophysiological pattern is consistent with a demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy

patient.chief_complaint: Ten-day progressive bilateral leg weakness, paresthesias, and facial diplegia with areflexia.

social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife and two children

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. H. is a 50-year-old man presenting to the emergency department with a 10-day history of progressive neurological symptoms. Approximately 3 weeks ago, he had a mild upper respiratory illness that resolved after 5 days. One week after recovery, he began noticing tingling in both feet. Over the following days, the tingling ascended to his knees and he developed progressive leg weakness — initially difficulty climbing stairs, then difficulty rising from a chair. By day 7, he noticed bilateral facial weakness and slurred speech. He presents today unable to walk without support. He has also noted dysphagia for thin liquids over the past 2 days and reports that his voice sounds 'nasal.' His wife noticed bilateral facial drooping which is now symmetric. He denies bladder dysfunction. He denies neck stiffness or fever. He has no history of tick exposure, recent travel, or toxin exposure. His symptoms have been progressive throughout with no fluctuation or improvement.

neurological_exam.additional: Respiratory: Forced vital capacity (FVC) measured at bedside: 2.2 L (predicted 3.8 L — 58% of predicted). NIF: -28 cmH2O. These values are concerning but not yet at intubation threshold.
neurological_exam.coordination: Cannot assess reliably due to weakness.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Bilateral facial weakness — forehead sparing absent (symmetric facial diplegia; upper and lower face involved). Dysarthria noted. Difficulty closing eyes fully bilaterally. All other cranial nerves intact.
neurological_exam.gait: Cannot stand without assistance. Too weak to attempt tandem gait.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and fully oriented. Anxious about his weakness.
neurological_exam.motor: Bilateral lower extremity weakness: hip flexion 4/5, knee extension 4/5, ankle dorsiflexion 3/5 bilaterally. Upper extremity: shoulder abduction 4/5, wrist extension 4/5, grip 4/5 bilaterally. Increased fatigue with sustained effort.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Absent deep tendon reflexes throughout: areflexia at bilateral biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, patellar, and Achilles. This is the most alarming finding.
neurological_exam.sensory: Bilateral distal lower extremity paresthesias (glove-and-stocking distribution). Mild reduction in vibration at bilateral ankles.
